why: It was the last of the 21 rules with no case, and a rule with no case is a rule nobody can refactor safely. The real failure is the repository that switches language halfway through: `prumo`, measured on 2026-08-30, has 24 files with Portuguese comments and 47 in English, and the next person writes in the language of the file they opened first. The floor is `min(pt, en) >= 3` on purpose — one stray English line in a Portuguese repository is a quotation, not a language switch — and the two sides exist to lock that floor from both directions: `pass` has FOUR files in Portuguese and zero in English, `fail` has the same four plus THREE in English, exactly the floor. Whoever lowers the floor to 1 leaves `pass` green and is not caught; whoever raises it to 4 turns `fail` green and is. The Portuguese in both trees is fixture, not prose: it is what the rule's PT stopword regex looks for, and translating it blinds the rule.
